rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidates, all resolve: chunk 2 line 10 'the repo you picked' -- cleared by the maintainer block's dated accept-note (line 92: '## Prework carries no instruction to do the prework and no locator... the section states what the prework left them holding'). Chunk 3 line 18 '**Fix** the bug tests-first' -- 'the bug' resolves against chunk 2 line 12 'The first bug fix here starts on the accountable side of that line', which precedes it in sequential order, and independently sits inside check_slides.md §1's own named carve-out list ('the bug from prework'). Chunk 7 line 61 'It is the simplest personal store' -- 'It' resolves to './CLAUDE.local.md' named at the start of the same bullet. Chunk 10 line 86 'Your rules file gets read' -- 'rules file' resolves against the LO at chunk 3 line 20 and the Key Concepts bullet at chunk 7 line 61, both earlier in the same file. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found anywhere in the body.

grep -niE for positional phrasing (above/below/earlier module/previous lecture/opening lecture/this workbook/at the top/further down) over the body returns two hits, neither a violation: line 34 'All modules are designed to cope with missing details from prior modules' is a general design statement about the training's construction, not a pointer at one specific unnamed earlier claim; line 86 'Your rules file gets read at the top of that session' is temporal (start of the M2 session), not page position -- confirmed by check-slide-deixis.js registering zero matches for this file (mechanical, rule 12, re-run below). Every cross-file link names its target in the link text itself: chunk 6 lines 40/42/44/46/48/50/52/54 (lecture/exercise titles as link text), chunk 9 lines 77/79/81/83 (author + title, e.g. 'The agentic engineering progression', 'Why Software Factories Fail'). No 'the opening lecture said' / 'above' / 'below' positional callback found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -niE 'you (did|saw|caught|ran|met|just)' over the body returns one hit: line 52's link text '[The machine you just met]' -- this is the linked lecture's own title carried through a structural include link (curriculum/CLAUDE.md: module files are 'thin: metadata + Bloom LOs + ordered refs'), the same class of link check_slides.md §13 rules out of scope ('Structural include-links... were never in scope; they are how the file gets inlined'). getting-going.md's own body prose makes no independent backward-beat CLAIM requiring resolution against the module's exercise/lecture set -- the lecture file the link points at owns that claim's truth, and is judged separately.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal instructional beat exists in this file -- it is a thin module index (metadata, LOs, links, concept recap), not a walked exercise or lecture demo. grep -niE 'guess|predict|before you (watch|see)' returns one hit, line 60 'the fix is a guess that happens to compile' -- generic engineering usage of 'guess' (an unverified fix), not a predict-then-reveal live-demo instruction. Nothing to check.

Word counts (check-slide-size.js): shortest chunks are 'Big Idea' (22w) and 'Next' (34w). Big Idea carries a self-standing claim ('Your first session should leave something behind that the next one can use. Otherwise you have a clever assistant and no compounding.'). Next carries two self-standing sentences (what M2 does; what carries forward). Neither is a wait-state or a single context-dependent fragment. No orphan found across all ten chunks.

All ten headers checked against their chunk content: Big Idea/Prework/What You'll Learn/How we work in this room/Freedom to choose/Start here/Key Concepts/Optional challenges/Pre-reads before Module 2/Next each match what the chunk actually delivers. Closest-to-tension case: 'Prework' with no imperative sentence inside it -- resolves via the maintainer's own accept-note (line 92) that the section reports what prework left the student holding, which is what a 'Prework' header truthfully promises here. No header contradicted by its own content.

Checked all six sub-tics against every chunk. 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' ban: only candidate is line 30 'Set the right pace for the group. Not too fast, not too slow.' -- one sentence, comma-joined pair, no third period-separated declarative -- not the banned triad shape. Anaphora/epistrophe: grep for repeated-structure triples over multi-sentence bullets (lines 33, 58, 59, 61) found none -- each is three distinct directives/claims, not a repeated grammatical frame. Self-grading superlatives: grep -niE 'one of the most|most useful|most important|the best way|incredibly useful' -> zero hits; line 61's 'the simplest personal store' grades CLAUDE.local.md's position in the personal/team/skill rule-file hierarchy (a technical-hierarchy fact), not the training's or exercise's own value -- not the value-prop-leak shape. Number+retraction: grep -niE 'about [0-9]|roughly|could be more|could be less' -> zero hits. Abstraction-noun stacks and empty-leg verb triplets: none found on inspection of every chunk.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: CONFIRMED FIXED. grep -c 'instruction surface' getting-going.md -> 0 (was 1, at chunk 8 line 71). grep -c 'the right rules file' getting-going.md -> 1, at line 71: 'Automate rule compounding. After each session, capture one evidenced lesson, route it to the right rules file, and check whether it helps next time.' Swept the whole body region (lines 1-87) for every dialect term the compendium names, plus adjacent repo-vocabulary risk (surface/firing/compendium/forcing function/beat/mood/Connections/judge/eval/sim/T0-T3/check_*.md/rule N/sponsor): every grep returned zero, cross-checked against a positive control (same terms DO appear, correctly, in the maintainer block at lines >=90, confirming the greps are live and not silently failing on a bad pattern). HARM CHECK: the fix names a concrete artefact the student already holds by this point in the module (CLAUDE.md / CLAUDE.local.md / a skill file, per the LOs at chunk 3 and Key Concepts at chunk 7) instead of the un-pointable abstraction 'instruction surface' -- the harm §8 exists to prevent (a room reading a term with no referent) is resolved, not relocated. NOT a trade into a different violation: 'rules file' is not on the banned list, and it is the same plain-English term this file already uses at line 20 ('a personal rules file at ./CLAUDE.local.md') and line 61 ('A ./CLAUDE.local.md built from session evidence...') -- the fix restores vocabulary consistency within the file rather than coining a new term.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 3 'What You'll Learn' bolds one verb per bullet -- exempt, module-shape.md's `- **[verb]** [thing]` LO template. Chunk 9 'Pre-reads' bolds only the mode word per entry (**Read:**, **Watch:**) -- exempt, named reading-list/menu carve-out. Chunk 6 'Start here' carries one bold ('**The question (to you):**') -- within the <=1 budget. Chunk 7 'Key Concepts' has zero bold. Chunk 4 'How we work in this room' bolds a short lead on all three bullets (**Make it work for you.**, **Exercises.**, **Everybody should be answering.**, each <=5 words) -- over the <=1-per-slide count on its face, but the compendium names this exact section by title as an open, undecided case ('Still genuinely open, not covered here: `## How we work in this room`'s bolded bullet leads, which no template mandates'). Per the dispatch preamble's harm-check, filing REVISE against a shape the compendium's own author has explicitly declined to rule on is not this judge's call -- carried forward as a rule question, not a finding, matching the prior pass's same call on the same chunk.
